problem_statement: Write a program to use a loop to find the factorial of a given number. The factorial of N is the product of all integers from 1 to N. Given Input: num = 5. Expected Output: 120.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses whether the algorithm's logic accurately computes the factorial for all valid non-negative integer inputs, including base cases.
sub_criteria: The algorithm correctly calculates the product of all integers from 1 up to the given input number.
The algorithm correctly produces a factorial of 1 when the input number is 0.
The algorithm correctly produces a factorial of 1 when the input number is 1.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates if all necessary structural components and steps are included to fully solve the problem as described.
sub_criteria: The algorithm includes a step to receive or define the input number for which the factorial is to be calculated.
The algorithm includes an initialization step for the variable that accumulates the factorial product.
The algorithm includes a loop structure that iterates through the sequence of numbers required for the factorial calculation.
The algorithm provides a clear final result for the calculated factorial.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: This dimension focuses on how easy the pseudocode is to understand and follow, ensuring logical steps are unambiguous.
sub_criteria: The logical flow of the algorithm is easy to follow step-by-step.
Variables and any named concepts in the pseudocode are clearly identifiable and have meaningful names.
Each step is described in a clear and unambiguous manner, allowing the reader to understand its purpose.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: This dimension examines the conceptual computational performance, ensuring the solution avoids obvious redundancies or unnecessary operations.
sub_criteria: The algorithm calculates the factorial using a single iterative pass through the necessary numbers.
The algorithm avoids redundant calculations or unnecessary storage of intermediate results.
